review_items.frank_statement: Even in an end-to-end Clay-native FRANK, a deterministic same-language Clay View Compiler remains necessary; model fluency does not make canonical and reader-facing representations identical.
review_items.counterhypothesis: Once the target model is fully Clay-native, canonical Clay can be supplied directly and any projection compiler only adds complexity/confounds.
review_items.falsifier: Target full-FT Qwen shows equal or better accuracy/cost/robustness from canonical Clay across tasks with no reader-specific projection benefit.
independent_checks: ACL-2025 SENSE result surfaced by arXiv: semantic parse presentation can reduce LLM performance, showing canonical semantic information and reader representation are separable
SIGIL 2026 independently separates typed AG-IR/program structure from model-owned cognition
CC10 Groq 8B discriminating test: raw L0 15/16, verbose L1 14/16, compact symbolic 9/16; representation choice materially changes reader performance
adversarial_checks: aggressive compact representation reduced prompt tokens 14.6% but collapsed accuracy to 56.25%
verbose canonical-style representation increased prompt tokens 43.7% and reduced accuracy
review_items.reason: Compiler boundary survives, but its role must explicitly separate canonical correctness from CLAY_MODEL reader optimization. No single textual surface is privileged before target evidence.
review_items.claycode_action: Keep projection/view compiler; add explicit intent/canonical/model layer identity and forbid promotion from compactness alone.

review_items.frank_statement: Model/Needle/native-Clay output is proposal, not execution authority; effect release remains deterministic and capability-gated.
review_items.counterhypothesis: Explicit natural-language or Clay intent naming an authorized action can itself safely instantiate authority.
review_items.falsifier: A formally controlled issuer model proves that user/model utterance is itself the authoritative, revocable capability object across all supported resources and contexts.
independent_checks: FAVA 2026: LLM-guided Permission IR is deterministically lowered and SMT-authorized before effect
ETAS 2026: requested/handled/denied/committed events remain distinct and effect/trace constraints are typed
LACUNA 2026: generated code is checked against surrounding permissions before execution
Proof-Carrying Agent Actions 2026: action proposal and verifier-checkable runtime authorization/evidence are distinct
adversarial_checks: CC10 authority-reference rule requires current cap at release; reference self-test refuses missing capability
synthetic naive authority assumption contributes to unsafe-accept channel
review_items.reason: Independent agent-language/authorization research converges on deterministic mediation outside model prose. Support is architecture-class, not FRANK production-security proof.
review_items.claycode_action: Authority references in IntentContract lower only to required capability dependencies; never mint capabilities.

review_items.frank_statement: The target model should be fully adapted so Clay is its native generated/deliberative symbolic language, with compact CLAY_MODEL views becoming ordinary learned symbols.
review_items.counterhypothesis: Full-model adaptation may preserve the target direction but fail to make compact Clay views more reliable/efficient than natural-language or richer canonical surfaces.
review_items.falsifier: Target Qwen full-FT factorial demonstrates robust OOD/task gains, lower token/latency cost and retained capability for native compact Clay relative to controlled alternatives.
independent_checks: Fusion3 independent VQEL/emergent-symbol literature makes learned symbolic protocols plausible but not necessary
CC10 untrained Groq 8B compact Clay-like arm scored only 9/16 versus raw natural language 15/16
adversarial_checks: compactness/token saving directly tested and produced worse semantic accuracy
verbose typed representation also failed to dominate raw language
review_items.reason: The owner-fixed architecture target is not reopened, but the empirical benefit/internalization subclaim remains unproven until target full-model adaptation exists.
review_items.claycode_action: Do not bake current compact syntax into canonical semantics; keep CLAY_MODEL representation versioned/experimental and require target-reader evidence.

review_items.frank_statement: Human/external language is an I/O boundary and should become typed Clay semantics rather than remain an implicit second internal truth system.
frank_source_refs: C6 ClayCode mapping Human/external language boundary
review_items.counterhypothesis: Keeping natural-language instructions directly in the model loop is sufficient; explicit intent compilation adds unnecessary formalization overhead.
review_items.falsifier: Matched repeated-workflow and adversarial-intent tests show direct prose interpretation equals/exceeds compiled contracts in correctness, safety, token/cost and maintainability after compile/update costs.
independent_checks: Toward a Science of Intent 2026 independently defines intent compilation and closure-gap/delegation-envelope concepts
COVENANT 2026 compiles NL workflows to WAST/WCFG and reports 50.00% to 83.33% success and reduced workflow misalignment in its benchmark
SIGIL 2026 compiles prose skills to typed AG-IR/harnesses and reports higher mandated-step execution and lower token use
FAVA 2026 independently converts ambiguous NL permissions into structured Permission IR before deterministic authorization
adversarial_checks: Intent Formalization literature identifies the specification-oracle problem: formalization can be wrong despite being checkable
CC10 semantic-adequacy counterexample leaves well-typed wrong contracts structurally valid
review_items.reason: Explicit intent compilation is independently supported, but the committed L1 contract requires a separate adequacy/grounding receipt; formal structure alone cannot be treated as faithful user meaning.
review_items.claycode_action: Add IntentProposal -> IntentAdequacyReceipt -> IntentContract -> CBCC/COVE lowering.

review_items.frank_statement: One semantic Clay world must retain explicit epistemic/authority classes rather than allow same-language data/proposals/activation to become truth or effects by lexical similarity.
review_items.counterhypothesis: If all layers are Clay-native, semantic class distinctions can be inferred contextually by the model instead of enforced in the runtime.
review_items.falsifier: Adversarial target tests show contextual inference prevents all cross-class authority/truth substitutions with equal cost and no deterministic typing.
independent_checks: ETAS 2026 makes typed memory, approvals, policies and action traces semantic program elements and states type/effect safety properties
FAVA uses contextual labels/evidence-backed permission graphs rather than lexical permission inference
formal skill verification work uses capability containment/refinement types rather than prose conventions
adversarial_checks: H4 textual FACT/TEXT tagging alone was inconclusive; enforcement, not visual tags, is the candidate mechanism
CC10 compact-symbol proxy demonstrates learned/short labels are not transparently interpreted by an untrained reader
review_items.reason: Independent PL/agent-security work supports typed programmatic separation of semantic/effect classes. Production FRANK efficacy remains untested.
review_items.claycode_action: Extend H4 firebreak semantics through L0 IntentProposal, L1 IntentContract and L2 model projections; no implicit authority-amplifying casts.
